newsitem.title: UK: Pillar, SITQ in deals, some with P&O.
newsitem.headline: Pillar, SITQ in deals, some with P&O.

text.p: Britain's Pillar Property Investments Plc said on Monday it had completed a number of retail-related property deals, some with Canadian pension fund SITQ, including two purchases of shopping centres from transport, and construction group Peninsular and Oriental Steamship Navigation Company (P&O).
The two P&O deals are worth a combined 37.15 million stg, while all five deals together commit a total of 70 million stg from Pillar and its SITQ partnership to retail-related property.

The PillarCaisse joint venture invests in UK shopping centres and the group said in a statement that the venture had bought Arndale Centres in Accrington and Leeds from P&O Shopping Centers "in an off-market transaction".

In the case of Accrington, the venture has bought the head leasehold interests for 17.15 million stg, while at Leeds it has paid 20 million stg for the freehold interest in the Cross Gates centre on an eight acre site.
The addition of these two centres brings the total number in the Pillar Caisse portfolio to eight, with a total capital value of about 200 million stg, the statement added.
In the other three deals, Pillar said it alone had completed contracts to buy two retail warehouse park investments in Wales and northwest England for a combined 25.3 million stg.
It has also exchanged contracts to fund a retail park development in southern Scotland "which will have an estimated value of 9.0 million stg".
"These transactions will bring Pillar's exposure in retail warehouse parks to 140 million stg," it added.

In comments on the deals, Pillar chairman Raymond Mould said "these deals further increase Pillar's already significant exposure to retail property and are an endorsement of our strategy of investing in high growth sectors."
Its overall portfolio is now 52 percent invested in shopping centres and retail warehouse parks.
